item.title: Billionaire wins appeal overturning A$23.4 million tax bill tied to Tasmania's Woolnorth dairy estate
item.description: A Full Court in Tasmania has overturned a significant tax assessment against companies related to Xianfeng Lu. The decision cancels a A$23.4 million stamp duty bill that included penalties and interest. This dispute originated from the 2016 purchase of the Woolnorth dairy estate, bought for A$280 million. The ruling removes a major financial liability for the companies managing the property in north-west Tasmania.

item.title: Shreveport's former Libbey Glass plant faces demolition, with 95% of materials set for recycling
item.description: Full-scale demolition of the former Libbey Glass plant in Shreveport is now underway and progressing. Environmental contaminants have been cleared over the 54-acre site, allowing for redevelopment opportunities. Demolition teams are set to dismantle the industrial silos that have dominated the skyline for decades. Local authorities expect increased truck traffic around Jewella Avenue until mid-2027 due to construction activities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iowa farmer turns to solar leases paying $1,200 per acre as falling crop prices squeeze profits
item.description: Tom Green, an Iowa farmer, backs the Folsom Lake Solar Project after it secured the green light from the Mills County Zoning Board. This initiative is set to ensure reliable income through long-term land leases amid tough farming conditions. It promises to produce a substantial amount of electricity, enough to power many local homes, while also creating jobs and boosting tax revenues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Robot sexually assaults 16-year old girl in Germany; 2 teens under probe
item.description: A teenage girl was allegedly groped by a humanoid robot while she was with friends. The incident occurred outside a fast-food restaurant in Cologne shortly after midnight. Police are investigating two young men believed to have recorded and livestreamed the event on social media. The robot, resembling Marvel's Iron Man, was discovered in a Volkswagen by authorities. Investigations are ongoing to determine the individuals responsible for controlling the robot.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Albania police use tear gas on protesting students as stir turns violent
item.description: In Albania, student protests escalated into violent clashes with police in the capital, Tirana. These demonstrations aimed to highlight critical issues surrounding education and socio-economic challenges. Students raised urgent concerns over campus conditions, rising tuition fees, and uncertain job prospects. Deputy Prime Minister Albana Koçiu denounced the unrest, advocating for peaceful expression. This incident reflects a wider wave of student activism sweeping across Europe, demanding systemic change.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: $2 photo of Billy the Kid valued at $5M
item.description: Randy Guijarro discovered an old photograph believed to include Billy the Kid in 2010, purchased for just $2. This photograph has been appraised at $5 million and may confirm its authenticity. After extensive research, experts linked the image to Billy the Kid’s social life during the late summer of 1878. The image also represents a more human side of the infamous outlaw.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Koos Bekker’s company controls 2,700 acres in Somerset, employs 650 locals as expansion sparks debate
item.description: In 2013, Koos Bekker's acquisition of Hadspen House sparked a transformative expansion into The Newt in Somerset, encompassing over 2,700 acres. This growth has generated local employment and attracted visitors, yet opinions remain divided. Many residents welcome the job opportunities, while others voice concerns about the estate's impact on community identity, land stewardship, and environmental sustainability, illustrating the complexity of fostering development without compromising local values.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya builds 400-company network to help refugees find jobs
item.description: Hamdi Ulukaya arrived in the United States in 1994, overcoming significant language and cultural obstacles. He founded Chobani, prioritizing the hiring of refugees to combat their employment challenges. In 2016, he initiated Tent to enhance job prospects for refugees within multiple industries. Collaborating with UNHCR, Ulukaya aims to forge connections between refugees and jobs, facilitating their economic incorporation into local communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California’s Rancho Cariñoso beachfront horse ranch sells for $22.55M after $109M asking price
item.description: Rancho Cariñoso was sold at auction for $22.55 million after previously being listed for $109 million. This estate features 4.2 acres of land and nearly an acre of private beachfront. The property includes a main house, equestrian facilities, and is near the Santa Barbara Polo Club. The auction indicated a significant discrepancy between initial valuation and buyer willingness to pay.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Kentucky man dies without a will, court awards widow half of $2.33 million accounts
item.description: A Kentucky appeals court has upheld a widow’s right to half of her late husband’s $2.33 million investment accounts, despite his children being named as beneficiaries. William E. Perrine died without a will in 2024. The court also ruled that his widow, Nancy, was entitled to half of $126,000 gifted to his children and grandchildren shortly before his death.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Oprah and Dwayne Johnson’s Maui fund distributed $60 million to over 8,100 fire survivors
item.description: Oprah Winfrey and Dwayne Johnson spearheaded the People’s Fund of Maui aimed at aiding wildfire survivors with financial support. Over $60 million was allocated to more than 8,100 affected residents during the recovery phase. Eligible adults were granted monthly payments of $1,200 to assist with essential needs. This initiative was created in conjunction with local elders and leaders, enabling survivors to focus on their most urgent requirements.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tiny Scottish island of Lismore uncovers evidence of a medieval Christian monastery
item.description: Residents of Lismore, a tiny Scottish island with around 190 inhabitants, raised funds for archaeological excavations that uncovered a medieval cemetery, ancient buildings and more than 1,000 metalworking artefacts. The discoveries suggest the island was an important religious and craft centre during the sixth and seventh centuries, shedding new light on early Christianity in northern Britain.

item.title: $2.8M in public funding protects a 58-acre Utah ranch from development while cattle continue grazing
item.description: Secured through public funding, a 58-acre ranch in Heber Valley, Utah, is preserved to avert urban sprawl. The Flying A Ranch Preserve will remain dedicated to agriculture, supporting cattle grazing and hay production. The conservation project, supported by nearly $2.8 million in various funding, is crucial for preserving local wildlife habitats and protecting vital water recharge systems, while aiming to safeguard additional farmland in the vicinity.
